Q: Choosing the best AI coding assistant for reasoning vs speed vs workflow efficiency A:

I have been on a non-stop research spree ever since I posted the query, and to be honest, I have found out there isn’t really a single tool that excels equally at reasoning, speed, and workflow integration — they tend to specialize.

Based on practical use:

  • Claude Code is stronger for reasoning-heavy tasks like structuring logic, explaining code, or handling multi-step problems

  • Cursor is better for day-to-day coding speed, especially inline edits and quick iterations inside your editor

  • Windsurf is still evolving, but it’s trying to combine both approaches

Tools like Claude tend to give more structured suggestions (e.g., adding validation, logging, or clearer decomposition), while Cursor is faster for quick inline tweaks.

If you’re trying to decide based on real workflows rather than features, this Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf comparison breaks down when each one is actually useful:

In practice, a lot of developers end up using:

  • one tool for thinking/debugging

  • another for speed during implementation

So the “best” choice depends on which part of your workflow you want to optimize most.

Q: move transition animation in gridlayout A:

Layouts don't have transitions, but views have e.g. ListView. There is also a GridView available.

Q: msgpack gem failing to install on MacOS when running `bundle install` A:

Inspired by these similar questions, and this blog post, I managed to get this gem to install by suppressing the particular C warnings that were causing the install to error:

gem install msgpack -v 1.4.2 --source 'https://rubygems.org/' -- --with-cflags="-Wno-compound-token-split-by-macro -Wno-incompatible-function-pointer-types"

Notice how the -Wno-* flags reference the warning IDs from the error output above.

Q: How to remember multiple tabs' session in terminal? (Alike FF session manager) A:

I used termit for about 15 years and now it stopped working for me, on my computer.

My replacement is the new Gnome terminal ptyxis where I run scripts like this:

ptyxis --tab --title "my tab" -d ~/dev/my/project
ptyxis --tab --title "src"    -d ~/dev/my/project/src
ptyxis --tab --title "docs"   -d ~/dev/my/project/docs

I run these scripts via an fzf selection picker in a script I called to

#!/bin/sh

# Open and run a terminal workspace script
selected=$(
  find ~/.local/share/terminal-workspaces/ -type f |
    fzf \
      --height=~200 \
      --select-1 \
      --highlight-line \
      --header="Open terminal workspace"
)
. $selected

So I'm opening up the new Gnome terminal (ptyxis), run to, select the workspace, hit enter and I'm ready to go!

Q: Weighted Score in Excel A:

I think you should develop a tool to make this calculations. I've adapted your needs to create a customizable calculator so you can play with rules like Higher or Lower and also custom coefs:

Let me explain how this works.

RULE row is just text values showing if that column is higher the better (H) or lower is better (L).

COEFS row is just a ratio to show how important is that variable in your calculations. Make sure they all sum up 100% or it won't work!

REFERENCE VALUE is to show the most important value in that column following rule indicated above (H or L). If the rule is H, the reference value is MAX of the column, else is 1-MIN of the column.

In this example I've manually forced and sorted values in each column. Notice all columns with rule H are values sorted descending order and columns with rule L are values sorted ascending order. You can see values highlighted in yellow color. Those values are the best option in that column (following RULE H or L)

RESULT column is your desired output. For each row, it divides the value (or 1-value if rule is L) of each column with their respective REFERENCE value (to calculate a ratio) and then multiply by the related coefs.

So for yellow row (forced manually to be the best values) RESULT is 1 because that row is the best of the best (normally you won't see that).

Now the formulas I've used:

RULE and COEFS are manual inputs to customize the behaviour. Trust me, is worth it.

REFERENCE VALUE: Formula in cell D6 is =IF(D2="H";MAX(D9:D23);1-MIN(D9:D23)). Drag to right

RESULT: Formula in cell K9 is =SUMPRODUCT(SI($D$2:$J$2="H";D9:J9;1-D9:J9)/$D$6:$J$6*$D$4:$J$4). Drag down.

I've tested with random values and it works awesome. You can even change rules H or L and customize coefs based on your needs.

I've uploaded and example to Google Drive just in case you want to check it.
